To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fungal and bacterial communities of Populus roots differ significantly among soils, and that the structure of fungal-bacterial networks differs among soil types, but not among Populus genotypes.

soil and plant genotype have significant impacts on fungal and bacteria communities in Populus rhizospheres and that fungal-bacterial networks are impacted by soil properties, but not by plant genotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of soil and plant genotypic effects on fungal-bacterial interactions in the Populus root microbiome.
the role that plant genotype and soil properties have in shaping the plant root-associated microbiome.
the role of soil and plant host on the assembly of the plant rhizosphere microbiome and the fungal-bacterial interactions therein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soil and host genotype are the main drivers of fungal-bacterial networks.
soil and plant genotype are important factors in shaping the belowground plant rhizobiomes, and that fungal-bacterial networks are important for understanding the belowground plant microbial ecology.
the fungal-bacterial networks of the plant microbiome are shaped by soil properties and host genotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soil properties, plant genotype and plant-fungus-bacterium interactions all contribute to the assembly of fungal and bacterial communities associated with plant roots.
soil and plant genotype are the most important factors influencing fungal-bacterial networks.
plant genotype and soil origin and chemical properties are important factors in shaping fungal and bacterial community composition in the Populus belowground microbiome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil properties, plant genotype, and fungal-bacterial interactions are all important factors shaping the plant microbiome.
plant genotype, soil properties and plant microbiomes are all interdependent.

soil properties and plant genotype are both significant determinants of root fungal and bacterial community structures, and that the plant genotype has a greater impact on the bacterial community than on the fungal community.
